comparison.objective: Punches a wire onto a 110 block with the cutting side toward the loose end; candidate fractures and recovers HELICOIL tangs.
comparison.physical_skill: Both use a narrow tool and localized axial loading, but punch-down requires wire positioning, terminal seating, and oriented trimming; candidate requires a separately held mandrel, separate hammer, notch fracture, withdrawal, and fragment recovery.
comparison.success_condition: The record lacks body and detailed scoring, but its title requires a seated/cut wire with correct tool orientation; candidate requires four free tangs contained and all inserts retained without damage.
comparison.reason: This is the closest impact-tool record, yet its central outcome is insulation-displacement termination and trimming, not bimanual hammer-driven notch fracture followed by recovery of independent fragments.
